content: The title of the page should be formatted as (Disease name) risk factors, with only the first letter of the title capitalized. The purpose of this page is to outline risk factors, which are behaviors or conditions that increase the likelihood of a patient developing a specific disease. A risk factor is defined as anything that raises an individual's probability of developing a disease. While risk factors often influence the development of a disorder, they do not directly cause the disorder in most cases. It is important to distinguish between risk factors and causes. Risk factors are correlational and not necessarily causal, as correlation does not imply causation. For instance, being young does not cause measles, but younger individuals are more likely to contract measles because they may not have developed immunity during a prior epidemic. Similarly, childhood obesity is a risk factor for diabetes but is not the direct cause of the disease. In contrast, HIV is the direct cause of AIDS, and the bacterium Bartonella henselae is the cause of cat scratch disease. When creating microchapter pages that link to the main page, include the following at the top of the edit box: `{{CMG}}`, your name template, and the microchapter navigation template you created earlier. Ensure that links within WikiDoc are created by placing brackets around key terms that you want to link to other pages. Make these links as specific as possible. For example, if a sentence includes the term anterior spinal artery syndrome, the link should direct to anterior spinal artery syndrome rather than generic terms like anterior, artery, or syndrome. For more information on creating links, refer to the relevant guidelines. Follow the formatting and capitalization rules outlined in the provided template. Additionally, include the name of the disease in the first sentence of every subsection. In the Overview section, the disease name should also appear in the first sentence. This section aims to summarize the risk factor page in a few sentences and may mirror the risk factors segment on the overview page. If one particular risk factor is strongly associated with the development of a disease, use statements such as: The most potent risk factor in the development of [disease] is [specific risk factor]. Other risk factors include [list additional factors]. If all risk factors contribute equally to disease development, use statements like: Common risk factors in the development of [disease] include [list factors]. On the Risk Factors microchapter page, use bullet points to list common risk factors. For example: Common risk factors in the development of [disease] include: [Risk factor 1] [Risk factor 2] If there are no known risk factors for the disease, state: There are no established risk factors for [disease]. You may also clarify the nature of the risk factors with statements such as: Common risk factors in the development of [disease] may be occupational, environmental, genetic, or viral. In the Common Risk Factors section, list the most frequently observed risk factors for the disease. This section may also include a table if appropriate. For guidance on inserting tables, refer to the relevant instructions. In the Less Common Risk Factors section, list the less frequently observed risk factors for the disease. This section may also include a table if necessary.
